summary:
Round 4. Accepted. Both round-3 findings are closed, and R3-1 is closed better than I proposed.

I proposed reordering verify() so check_recovery ran before the refusal precondition. The author declined that and attacked the emptiness instead, and the author is right: reordering fixes the ordering bug but a run reaching check_recovery would still carry refused == set(), so `recovered n refused = {}` would stay vacuous, merely later. The substitution drives the refusal path deliberately -- REFUSAL_PROBES = 12 appends with a truncated JSON body, refused with 400 at serde_json::from_slice before the handler touches the journal (server.rs:639), each body still carrying its key in its bytes so a recovered probe key can only mean the server stored a request it declined. No fault injection, no size-capped filesystem, no host dependency.

I verified it end to end rather than accepting the author's mutation report. Independent narrow mutation, client-side only, real binary and real kill and real restart untouched: append_raw rewritten so probe bodies are well-formed (the unpatched server stores them) while the client is told 400 (the contract records them as refused). Result: 'MUTANT KILLED BY THE RESURRECTION ASSERTION -- 12 appends the server explicitly refused with a non-2xx status came back after restart (first: ['m000000'...])'. The assertion reaches check_recovery and fires there, not on some earlier guard. My own clean run of HEAD then gave PASS with "refused": 12, "refusals_probed": 12, "submitted": 412 -- against "refused": 0 on every green run of the previous two digests. The promise clause 'every append the server refused with a non-2xx status is absent' is now evidenced by real members instead of satisfied by an empty set.

On the author's three scepticism targets. (1) Does the probe move the vacuity somewhere else: no. The set is non-empty in every green run, the assertion is not preempted -- duplicated and lost cannot fire on a probe key, and phantom is computed after it and would not catch a probe anyway since probe keys are in `sent` -- and the new precondition grades the accept direction too. (2) Can probe_refused != REFUSAL_PROBES be tripped by something other than the defect it targets: no, and I swept it -- 12/0 passes, 11/0 and 0/0 are red naming the accepted malformed body, 12/3 is red on the separate well-formed branch. A probe that goes unanswered raises out of the loop and aborts the run loudly rather than reaching this branch, so the branch is reachable essentially only by a server that accepted a malformed body. (3) Probes before the writers rather than interleaved: correct trade. Interleaving would buy refusals under concurrency at the price of a precondition that must tolerate unanswered probes, and any probe still in flight at the kill lands in `unknown`, not `refused`, so it would contribute nothing to the assertion. The exact precondition is worth more than the load coverage, and the choice is documented at :332-337 rather than left implied.

On shipping the weak instance while naming the strong one: I agree with the trade, and I checked the constraint rather than taking it. Degraded mode still has exactly one entry point -- AppState::persist discriminating on StorageFull (server.rs:206-214) -- with no external trigger, so refused-after-apply cannot be driven portably from outside the process, and a host-conditional case would be the false green this EC has spent four rounds removing. What matters is that the boundary is stated where a downstream reader sees it: the pyproject oracle text now says the probes are rejected at parse time before touching the journal, and the docstring at :110-116 names the sharp case, names where it must live, and names why it becomes central under group commit (a batch whose barrier fails must apply none of its members). That is a handoff to the TD, not a concealment.

R3-2 is closed: measure()'s warm-up checks the status and raises ContractFailure naming the connection level (:267-279), with the comment recording that the silence was introduced by the author's own append fix. Both non-blocking notes are addressed. INCUMBENT_OBSERVATIONS carries the fifth measurable observation (63.0, 87.6, 192.6) and the docstring table its sixth row.

Gates re-run by me from the repo root, not taken on report: 39 unit tests green across three files; aw ec check --project tape --wi 3052 clean (2 cases, 3 authored unit-test files); ec-3052-durability PASS with the facts above; ec-3052-scaling FAIL on ratio 1.08 against 4.0, which is the correct verdict against unmodified HEAD for a capability that does not exist yet, and green on both the floor and the ceiling.

The three checks that carry this EC are now each verified to be able to go red by something other than an argument. Ceiling: a genuine zero-durability tape (serve with neither --store nor --data-dir, so AppState.store is None and persist returns Ok(()) without a barrier, server.rs:188-190) measured 5069.6 ops/s at 1 connection against a 594.0 ceiling on my host, 8.5x over. Floor: check_scaling rejects a fixed-linger shape at fraction 0.102 with the ratio passing at 15.0, and is sharp at the constant, 0.24 red and 0.26 green. Resurrection: the mutant above. Every one of the four rounds' findings was that an assertion could not fire; none of the assertions in this digest has that property.

reviewer_kind is agent: this verdict is arbitration input for the human batch audit, not human acceptance evidence, and it authorizes only source_digest sha256:b9a13898...8394.
